takeoffs.strip_title: Compact strip — also show the conditions as a horizontal strip above the canvas (handy on small projects with the panel collapsed)

takeoffs.no_conditions: No conditions yet — add one and start tracing.
takeoffs.help_copy: Select a shape on the plan, then ⧉ Copy / ⎘ Paste (⌘C / ⌘V) — it lands on the sheet under your cursor.
takeoffs.help_undo: ⌫ undo point · Esc cancel · scroll = zoom · pan mid-measure: press-and-drag (a click without dragging places the point).
takeoffs.cond_title_active: Make this the active condition (double-click zooms to its takeoffs · ⌘-click / ⇧-click selects for bulk edit · drag to the top-bar palette for one-click access)
takeoffs.cond_title_reassign: Reassign selected shape to this condition
takeoffs.hotkey_title: Press {{num}} to activate (pin to lock this number)
takeoffs.twin_title: A twin — its materials follow another condition
takeoffs.twin_count_title: {{count}} material row(s) no longer follow(s) the family
takeoffs.zoom_title: Zoom the canvas to this condition's takeoffs

takeoffs.project_sigma_title: Σ = whole project, every sheet. The leading numbers count the open sheets only.
takeoffs.supporting_heading: Supporting Materials — order qty = measured ÷ coverage, rounded up.
takeoffs.twin_split_title: Split out — freeze the following rows where they stand and stop following "{{tag}}". Keeps its name and still groups with the family.
takeoffs.twin_follow_title: These materials follow "{{tag}}". Edit a row and only that row stops following.
takeoffs.duplicate_button_title: Duplicate this condition — the same finish measured somewhere else, with its own materials. Name the area (e.g. Level 2); no takeoffs come along, you measure into it, and its materials keep following this condition until you change them there.
takeoffs.mat_basis_seam_lf_title: Figured seam length from the roll layout — 0 until this condition carries a roll setup
takeoffs.mat_round_title: Round up to whole units (you buy whole buckets/bags)
takeoffs.mat_promote_title: Save this material to the library (this line becomes linked)
takeoffs.mat_revert_title: Revert this field to the library value
takeoffs.mat_linked_title: Linked to "{{name}}" in the material library — amber fields differ from the library values
takeoffs.mat_follow_title: Following {{tag}} — edit any field here and this row stops following (the others keep following)
takeoffs.mat_own_title: This row is this condition's own
takeoffs.mat_own_detached_title: This row is this condition's own — it no longer follows {{tag}}
takeoffs.mat_follow_button_title: Follow the family again — take this row's values back from {{tag}}
takeoffs.mat_restore_title: Put it back — takes the row from {{tag}} again
takeoffs.mat_attach_title: Attach a material from the library — the line copies the library values and stays linked
takeoffs.grout_derive_title: Start the grout calculator with standard tile geometry (12×24×3/8″ @ 1/8″, 25 lb bag) — REPLACES this line's coverage rate and note with the derived values
takeoffs.coverage_preset_title: Coverage preset — trowel notch / spread rate. Generic industry-typical values; verify against the product data sheet.
takeoffs.library_description: Reusable condition templates, shared across every plan in this browser. A fresh workspace seeds from this library (built-in flooring defaults when it's empty).
takeoffs.library_save_title: Snapshot the active condition (appearance, waste, H/T, materials) into the library
takeoffs.library_save_default: + save the active condition to the library
takeoffs.library_empty: No templates yet — make a condition the way you like it, then save it here.
takeoffs.library_apply_title: Add a condition from this template to the takeoff
takeoffs.library_delete_title: Remove this template from the library
takeoffs.materials_description: Reusable materials, browser-wide. Attaching one to a condition copies its values and keeps a link — edits here only reach linked lines when you push them.
takeoffs.materials_empty: No library materials yet — add one below, or use "→ lib" on a condition's material line.
takeoffs.materials_push_title: Replace the values on every linked condition line with these library values (overrides included)
takeoffs.materials_remove_title: Remove from the library — linked lines keep their values, only the link is removed
takeoffs.columns_shape_labels_desc: Phase / area labels (e.g. Phase 1, East Wing) for grouping the Report by shape.
takeoffs.columns_label_rename_title: Rename this label — labeled shapes follow
takeoffs.columns_label_remove_title: Remove from the list — labeled shapes keep the value (shown ungrouped in the Report)
takeoffs.columns_add_value_title: Add this value to the list
takeoffs.columns_description: Custom columns (e.g. CSI Division) classify conditions for report grouping and exports. Columns and values apply to the whole project; assign values on a condition in the Takeoffs tab.
takeoffs.columns_empty: Add a column, e.g. CSI Division.
takeoffs.columns_value_rename_title: Rename this value — assigned conditions follow
takeoffs.columns_value_remove_title: Remove from the list — conditions keep the value, shown as (removed)
takeoffs.transitions_disabled_title: Two finishes with measured rooms on the open sheets are needed before anything can meet.
takeoffs.transitions_enabled_title: Derive where two finishes meet onto {{tag}}. Runs where the rooms butt inside one open space commit dashed, pending Accept; runs across a wall are reported and never counted — that transition is a threshold in a doorway no trace can locate.
takeoffs.transitions_runs_committed: {{count}} run(s) · {{lf}} LF proposed on {{tag}} — dashed until you Accept.
takeoffs.transitions_no_joints: No butt joints between these two on the open sheets.
takeoffs.transitions_reported_title: These rooms are adjacent across a partition. The transition is a threshold in the doorway, and nothing in the trace record says where the doorway is — so it is reported, never counted. Measure it at the door.
takeoffs.transitions_look_title: Center the sheet on this run — find the door and measure the threshold there
takeoffs.transitions_footnote: Adjacent, not joined — measure the threshold at the door.

agent.title: Agent
agent.configured_intro: The agent runs on a model you provide — your endpoint, your key, straight from this browser (the same bring-your-own-AI seam as the scale reader). Nothing is configured, so it can't run.
agent.configured_desc: Once configured, you describe a takeoff ("take off the carpet per the finish schedule on this sheet") and the agent aims the app's own tools — the text layer, the schedule parser, the one-click engine — then stages dashed proposals you accept or reject. It never invents geometry and never commits anything itself.
agent.placeholder: e.g. "Take off the carpet per the finish schedule on this sheet."
agent.status_working: Working — proposals land as dashed outlines.
agent.accept_all_title: Accept every visible proposal (⏎ on the canvas does the same)
agent.reject_all_title: Discard every pending proposal (local only — nothing is recorded)
agent.accept_title: Accept — commits as a takeoff (origin: agent, human-reviewed)
import.title: Import from schedule — {{count}} finish(es) found
import.skipped: {{count}} row(s) skipped (couldn't be read as a single finish)
ai.title: AI — bring your own key
ai.description: OpenTakeoff can ask a vision model you provide to read things off the plan — starting with the drawn scale when the sheet text doesn't state one. Point it at an OpenAI-style or Anthropic-style endpoint: a hosted API, or a local runtime on your own machine (most local runtimes speak the OpenAI style and need no key).
ai.privacy_note: What's sent, and only when you click an AI button: a snapshot of the sheet region in question, plus the question. Never the whole plan file, file names, project names, or your takeoff.
ai.field_api_key: API key (leave blank for local runtimes)
ai.storage_note: The key is stored in this browser (localStorage) — anyone with access to this browser profile can read it, so use a key you can revoke. Leave everything blank and the AI features stay out of your way entirely. The endpoint must allow requests from a browser (CORS); local runtimes generally allow localhost.
layer.title: Layers
layer.description: What the drawing states each ink is — feeds One-Click and room detection on these sheets. Wall stops a fill, Off is passed through, Auto follows the stated role. The sheet itself draws unchanged.
layer.wall_title: Wall — treat this layer's ink as hard boundary (a fill stops at it)
layer.off_title: Off — ignore this layer's ink entirely (a fill passes through it)
layer.reset_title: Return every layer on this sheet to Auto
account.title: Account — {{email}}
status.stale_tab: OpenTakeoff was updated in another tab — reload this tab to continue.
home.title: Projects
home.no_projects: No projects yet — create a folder in the Projects drive.
roll.title: Roll goods
roll.empty: No roll-goods conditions yet. Open a condition's properties in the Takeoffs panel and add a roll setup (carpet, sheet vinyl, rubber) — its floor areas get figured into cuts here.
roll.cuts_show_title: Draw the figured cuts over the plan
roll.edit_title: Edit cuts on the plan — drag a cut along its lane, pull its ends to resize; double-click resets a cut to the figured layout
roll.multiplier_title: The condition's ×N applies to the ORDER — the diagram shows one unit's cuts
roll.oversize: A cut is longer than one whole roll — it needs a cross-seam the math can't place. Split the run on the plan (edit mode) or raise the max roll length.
roll.drag_hint: Drag a cut on the roll to change the cutting order — the roll re-packs.
roll.reset_order_title: Clear the manual cutting order — the packer sequences widest-then-longest again
takeoffs.cond_multiplier_title: Multiply this condition by N identical units (measure one, ×N)
takeoffs.cond_waste_title: Waste % — a flooring allowance added on top of the measured quantity in the Report. You choose it per condition (e.g. ~8% straight-lay LVP, ~15% diagonal, ~20% herringbone).
takeoffs.style_title: Line style — the outline dash for this finish's floor-area and linear takeoffs (canvas + Marked Set PDF). Surface walls and deducts keep their own dashing.
takeoffs.height_title: Height ({{unit}}) — the default for NEW wall traces (SF = LF × H) and the vertical-SF display on floor areas. Walls keep the height they were drawn at — select a wall to change just that one.
takeoffs.thickness_title: Thickness ({{unit}}) — a Linear run with thickness also computes border/feature-strip SF = LF × T/12. Changing it re-flows existing linear runs.
takeoffs.classify_title: Classify this condition — the Report can group and export by these (manage columns in the Columns tab)
takeoffs.roll_optin_title: Make this condition a roll-goods material — its floor areas get figured into roll cuts (seams, order footage, a cut diagram)
takeoffs.roll_setup_title: Roll-goods setup — the engine figures seams, cuts, and order footage from this condition's floor areas
takeoffs.roll_material_title: Material class — sets the cut overlay's material-true color
takeoffs.roll_remove_title: Remove the roll-goods setup (cuts and order footage stop being figured; manual cut edits on shapes are kept but inert)
takeoffs.roll_width_resilient_title: Roll width — resilient sheet widths vary by product (6′, 6′6″, 12′…)
takeoffs.roll_max_title: Max usable length of one physical roll — 0 = continuous (cut off one roll). When set, cuts pack across rolls and the diagram marks the roll breaks.
takeoffs.roll_direction_title: Run direction — auto picks whichever needs less footage; force it when the pattern or the light dictates
takeoffs.roll_seam_title: Seam allowance — extra width where two cuts meet, per seamed edge
takeoffs.roll_unit_title: The unit this material sells in — a unit, never a dollar (the takeoff stays quantities-only)
takeoffs.roll_figured_title: The figured order — how far down the roll the cuts reach (side-by-side cuts share length), rounded up to the inch. The Roll panel has the cut diagram.
takeoffs.spec_title: Product spec imported from the finish schedule — editable; shown as read-only columns in the Report / CSV / XLSX
